source.title: Loss Landscape Dependent Self-Adjusting Learning Rates in Decentralized Stochastic Gradient Descent
source.authors: Wei Zhang; Mingrui Liu; Yu Feng; Xiao-Dong Cui; Brian Kingsbury; Yu-Hai Tu

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; some table cells appear flattened or corrupted (for example, Table 1 contains “10” in cells described in prose as divergence).
record.tranche_reason: The study compares held-out performance under large-batch decentralized and synchronous SGD, testing batch-size effects under a different optimizer intervention from the claim’s cited studies.
record.gate_note: The paper reports held-out accuracy/loss under varying batch sizes and optimizer conditions. Its large-batch comparisons bear on V5. Flatness plots and Hessian projections are not the magnitude-aware perturbation measure in V7. Random-label fitting, architecture comparisons, width sweeps, adaptive optimizers, dropout, and memorized-example removal are not tested. Cited results are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: Fixed-epoch CIFAR-10 and ImageNet experiments measure held-out performance across batch sizes and test decentralized SGD as a recipe adaptation. Appendix F explicitly confirms equal epoch budgets. Acoustic speech-recognition models are outside V5's image-classifier and language-model scope.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the conclusion: in large-batch, large-learning-rate settings, DPSGD can match convergent SSGD and converge when SSGD diverges. The authors attribute this to intrinsic landscape-dependent noise that adjusts the effective learning rate, supported by their theory and experiments.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares decentralized parallel SGD with synchronous SGD, using 16 learners and task-specific large-batch learning-rate schedules; the claim’s cited large-batch studies use other interventions and comparison setups.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with batch size, learning rate, task, and model. The paper reports SSGD divergence at particular large-batch settings; reducing learning rate or adding tuned Gaussian noise can permit some SSGD runs to converge, generally with worse results than DPSGD.

fits_no_version.finding: DPSGD prevents large-batch divergence on SWB acoustic-model tasks where synchronous SGD fails.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large-batch acoustic-model training can lose held-out performance under synchronous SGD, and decentralized SGD can avoid this failure under the same epoch budget.

fits_no_version.finding: MNIST optimizer comparisons show convergence and test-error differences at a fixed batch setting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Decentralized SGD's intrinsic noise can improve convergence and held-out accuracy relative to synchronous SGD or fixed Gaussian weight noise.

fits_no_version.finding: Contour and Hessian visualizations associate flatter solutions with better test performance without measuring magnitude-aware sharpness or ranking generalization gaps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the tested optimizer comparisons, decentralized SGD can find visually flatter solutions with better held-out performance.

record.peer_reviewed: AAAI 2022 copyright notice appears in the text; venue metadata supplied for this record is arXiv.org.
record.problems: The reported experiments focus on optimizer convergence and held-out performance, not the training-test gap itself. Several results are qualitative or shown in figures; the flattened tables contain ambiguous cells. No uncertainty estimates are stated.
record.rows_left_out: Detailed per-model CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-1K table entries, plus additional batch-size and learning-rate comparisons, were not extracted. Table 1 and Table 9 are flattened and contain ambiguous cell alignment; the retained rows prioritize stated aggregate outcomes and explicit divergence cases. The study's additional contour and Hessian visualizations are not the magnitude-aware measure specified in V7.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Controlled convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and learned local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under the specified tuning regimes; the LAMB runtime illustration does not establish this comparison.
Language models, longer-training remedies, and controlled normalization or regularization interventions. The study does test fixed epoch budgets; that aspect should not be listed as untested.
Magnitude-aware training-error perturbation tolerance, its association with training-test gaps, and comparison against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removal of memorized examples followed by retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The main extraction error is treating optimizer superiority as the batch-size effect. Fixed epoch budgets are explicitly confirmed in Appendix F. Detailed batch sweeps and tuning results are already declared in rows_left_out, so they are not newly missing. No verdict is warranted for V7 or for language models.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under different tuning choices.
Language models; longer training; normalization or regularization changes; comparisons under fixed epoch budgets across the full set of batch sizes and workload-dependent thresholds.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance and comparison against norm- and margin-based measures.

rows.subject: CIFAR-10 tasks (10 CNN models; aggregate as reported)
rows.size_stated: 10 CNN models; individual sizes listed in Table 6
rows.operation_detail: Compared SSGD and DPSGD at batch size 8192 with learning rate 0.8; same epoch schedule.
rows.baseline: SSGD; batch size 128 baseline is presented for reference
rows.value: DPSGD outperforms SSGD in all but one case; SSGD diverges on EfficientNet-B0 and SENet-18.
rows.locator: Section 4, “SSGD and DPSGD Comparison on CIFAR-10”; Table 1
rows.note: The paper reports the aggregate comparison and names the two divergence cases; individual values are omitted here because the flattened table contains ambiguous cells.
rows.check: The aggregate optimizer comparison mixes batch penalties and their mitigation; it cannot have one directional state. Split by model and optimizer, comparing smaller and larger batches. Table 1's 10% entries are valid chance-level accuracies consistent with divergence, not corrupted cells. This aggregate also duplicates R2 and R3.

rows.subject: EfficientNet-B0
rows.operation_detail: Compared SSGD and DPSGD at batch size 8192 with learning rate 0.8; same epoch schedule.
rows.baseline: SSGD diverges; batch size 128 baseline accuracy 87.51%
rows.locator: Section 4, “SSGD and DPSGD Comparison on CIFAR-10”; Table 1; Noise-injection and Learning Rate Tuning
rows.note: The paper explicitly states SSGD diverges on this task; it also gives the DPSGD test accuracy.
rows.check: For the DPSGD subject, accuracy rises from the batch-128 reference of 87.51% to 91.13% at batch 8192, reversing the batch penalty relative to that reference. Record SSGD separately: its batch-8192 accuracy is 10%, showing a penalty. The DPSGD result supports the adaptation clause; it does not establish that increasing batch size alone improves accuracy.

rows.subject: SENet-18
rows.operation_detail: Compared SSGD and DPSGD at batch size 8192 with learning rate 0.8; same epoch schedule.
rows.baseline: SSGD diverges; batch size 128 baseline accuracy 95.18%
rows.locator: Section 4, “SSGD and DPSGD Comparison on CIFAR-10”; Table 1; Noise-injection and Learning Rate Tuning
rows.note: The paper explicitly names SSGD divergence and reports the DPSGD accuracy.
rows.check: DPSGD accuracy at batch 8192 is 90.48%, below the batch-128 reference of 95.18%, so a batch penalty remains despite adaptation. Record SSGD's 10% accuracy separately. Comparing DPSGD only against divergent SSGD measures optimizer rescue rather than the batch penalty.

rows.subject: ImageNet-1K tasks (6 CNN models; aggregate as reported)
rows.operation_detail: Compared SSGD and DPSGD under large-batch linear learning-rate scaling with warmup; 100 epochs.
rows.value: SSGD diverges for AlexNet, VGG11, and VGG11-BN; DPSGD converges.
rows.locator: Section 4, “SSGD and DPSGD Comparison on ImageNet-1K”; Appendix E, “ImageNet-1K Training Progression”; Table 9
rows.note: The text identifies three SSGD divergence cases; overall SSGD and DPSGD are described as comparable in the large-batch setting.
rows.check: Split the aggregate by model and optimizer and include the batch-256 references. At batch 8192, SSGD reaches 0.10% top-1 accuracy on AlexNet, VGG11 and VGG11-BN; DPSGD reaches 49.01%, 65.00% and 63.55%, respectively, versus references of 56.31%, 69.02% and 70.65%. Both methods retain penalties for these models, although DPSGD avoids divergence. AlexNet and VGG11 already diverge under SSGD at batch 4096.

rows.subject: SWB-300 LSTM task
rows.operation_detail: Compared SSGD and DPSGD with large batches using the stated warmup and annealing schedule.
rows.baseline: SSGD diverges beyond batch size 2048; divergence loss 10.37
rows.value: DPSGD converges through batch size 8192; held-out loss 1.66
rows.locator: Section 4, “SSGD and DPSGD Comparison on ASR tasks”; Table 3
rows.note: The study reports fixed training epochs for each task and explicitly states the divergence threshold.
rows.check: SWB-300 is acoustic classification of context-dependent HMM states, not language modeling or image classification. Its held-out loss therefore does not measure V5's named systems. The numerical comparison is otherwise supported. Epoch descriptions conflict: Section 4 describes a 20-epoch schedule, while Appendix D specifies 16 epochs.

rows.subject: SWB-2000 LSTM task
rows.operation_detail: Compared SSGD and DPSGD with large batches using the stated warmup and annealing schedule.
rows.baseline: SSGD diverges beyond batch size 4096; divergence loss 10.37
rows.value: DPSGD converges through batch size 8192; held-out loss 1.47
rows.locator: Section 4, “SSGD and DPSGD Comparison on ASR tasks”; Table 3
rows.note: The study reports fixed training epochs for each task and explicitly states the divergence threshold.
rows.check: SWB-2000 is an acoustic model, outside V5's named systems. Its numerical comparison is supported, but it cannot establish a language-model result. The same 16-versus-20-epoch inconsistency applies.

rows.subject: MNIST fully connected network (SSGD)
rows.size_stated: Two hidden layers, 50 units per layer
rows.operation_detail: Compared with DPSGD at large batch and learning rate; fixed-noise SSGD* also evaluated.
rows.locator: Section 2, “The Landscape-dependent Self-Adjusting Learning Rate in DPSGD Help Convergence”; Figure 2(a)
rows.note: This is an illustrative large-batch convergence comparison, not a controlled test of test-error gaps across fixed epoch budgets.
rows.check: This compares optimizers at one batch size and learning rate, without a smaller-batch reference. It demonstrates convergence differences, not V5's batch-size penalty.

rows.subject: MNIST fully connected network (SSGD*)
rows.size_stated: Two hidden layers, 50 units per layer
rows.operation_detail: Added Gaussian weight noise with constant variance; noise strength was fine-tuned.
rows.locator: Section 2, “The Landscape-dependent Self-Adjusting Learning Rate in DPSGD Help Convergence”; Figure 2(a)
rows.note: The paper says only fine-tuned constant-noise SSGD converged and that its solution was inferior.
rows.check: Tuned constant-noise SSGD versus DPSGD at one batch size measures optimizer performance. No smaller-batch comparison establishes V5.

rows.subject: MNIST fully connected network (DPSGD)
rows.size_stated: Two hidden layers, 50 units per layer
rows.operation_detail: Compared with SSGD at a smaller learning rate; decentralized learners average neighboring weights.
rows.locator: Appendix C, “Appendix for the effect of DPSGD noise in help finding flat minima with better generalization”; Figure 5
rows.note: This is a smaller-learning-rate comparison; both algorithms converge.
rows.check: The 2.3% versus 2.6% test-error comparison holds the training setup fixed while changing optimizer. It neither varies batch size nor measures V7's magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance or ranking of generalization gaps.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10 EfficientNet-B0, batch 8192 with decentralized SGD
relationships.reason: R2 shows the adapted recipe avoids the penalty relative to batch 128: 91.13% versus 87.51%; synchronous SGD instead reaches 10%. This supports V5's recipe-adaptation clause.
relationships.display_finding: Decentralized SGD achieved higher accuracy than the small-batch reference, but this comparison remains unverified.

relationships.reason: R3 retains a penalty under DPSGD, 90.48% versus 95.18% at batch 128, while improving substantially over synchronous SGD's 10%.
relationships.display_finding: Performance improved substantially over synchronous SGD but remained below the small-batch result; these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: ImageNet AlexNet, VGG11 and VGG11-BN, batch 8192 with warmup and linear scaling
relationships.reason: R4, supplemented by Tables 2 and 9 in the text, shows synchronous SGD divergence and DPSGD accuracies still below the batch-256 references; adaptation reduces but does not remove these penalties.
relationships.display_finding: Synchronous training diverged, and decentralized training still had accuracy deficits, but these comparisons remain unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Large-batch CIFAR-10, ImageNet-1K, and ASR tasks under the reported schedules
reader_labels.reason: DPSGD avoids several SSGD divergence cases at batch size 8192, but CIFAR-10 results are described as outperforming SSGD in all but one case, ImageNet accuracy as comparable overall, and the study does not test the claim’s broader fixed-epoch comparisons across batch sizes (R1–R6).
